frase_gancho.texto: A seated man, shaped as a vessel, who seems to be thinking about something.

puente_narrativo.texto: From the vessel, we move on to a small jewel. Look for a pendant shaped like a turtle, made of tiny pieces of turquoise set onto a seashell, hanging from a long necklace of beads.

guion_corto.texto: This clay vessel, about seventeen centimeters tall, comes from the Casas Grandes region in Chihuahua, and it was made some eight hundred years ago. It takes the shape of a seated man, curled up on himself, in a posture that seems thoughtful. His body and face are covered with red and black lines on a cream background, which have been interpreted as body paint or tattoos. It is a vessel and a sculpture at the same time: the liquid poured out through an opening in the head or the back. In Paquimé, people made vessels shaped like humans, birds, and other animals. It is thought that this one represents an ancestor, a shaman, or an important figure of the city.

guion_largo.texto:
After so many pots with round shapes, this one sits down to look at you. It is a vessel with a face, made with such care that it almost looks like a portrait. And it is not the only one of its kind: the people of Paquimé made many vessels shaped like people and animals, and each one has something of its own.

Many have been found in tombs. It is thought that in this adobe city, important dead were buried beneath the floors of houses, along with their offerings: seashells, necklaces, polished axes, and turquoise stones. If so, the ancestors kept on living beneath the family ground. A vessel in the shape of a person would then have served to accompany the one who was departing.

The red and black lines on the body may have represented body paint used in ceremonies. It is the same idea you saw in the [Tamuín Adolescent](mna_s08_adolescente_huasteco) and in the [Ixtlán couple](mna_s10_pareja_ixtlan): the body as a page on which is written who you are and what role you have. Here we know little about what the drawings meant, but we do know they were not simple decoration.

Notice the posture. The curled-up body, the lowered head, and a calm attitude give the figure an air of reflection that is almost never seen in ancient art, where warriors, gods, and rulers abound. Is it a real man, an ancestor, a shaman? All three ideas have been proposed, and the truth is that we do not know. What is lovely is that, eight hundred years later, the figure still looks thoughtful.

Paquimé was a frontier city, and it shows in its customs. It had adobe houses like those of the peoples of the Southwest, but also ball courts like those of Mesoamerica, and mounds shaped like birds and serpents. It is thought that its inhabitants took ideas from both sides and blended them in their own way. This vessel, with its very personal look, is an example.

And the art of Paquimé was not entirely forgotten. Today, in the town of Mata Ortiz, near Casas Grandes, there are potters who recovered the style of the ancient ceramics. It is said that it all began with Juan Quezada, who learned by observing the ancient fragments he found in the countryside. The past inspired hands once again.

One last observation. Because the opening is in the head or the back, to pour the liquid you had to tilt the figure. It is a curious gesture: the clay person bows and gives a drink. Perhaps it is no coincidence, perhaps it is; what is certain is that it joins the useful object with the human image in a very elegant way.

The north does not end with this piece. There are still jewels, vessels that sound, models of sites, and rock paintings. But you can already see the essentials: from the hunters of the desert to the adobe cities, the north was a land of ingenious people with long memories. And that past did not disappear: many of those peoples are still here, with their languages, their festivals, and their way of seeing the world.

texto: Look for the opening through which the liquid was poured
Follow the red and black lines on its body and face
Observe its posture: what do you think it is thinking?

texto.Period: Postclassic / Middle Period of Paquimé (1100-1300 AD)
texto.Material: Modeled clay with polychrome geometric decoration in red and black

texto.pregunta: Myth: Vessels shaped like humans were simple toys or decorations.
texto.respuesta: Reality: They were containers and sculptures at the same time, and they have been found in tombs, alongside offerings. It is thought that they represented ancestors or important figures.
